data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference is defensible as a 'critical rationalist imperative': we prefer the theory that has withstood our best efforts to destroy it, not because it is true, but because it is the only one currently worthy of serving as a basis for further criticism.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If acting on a theory requires more than just using it as a target (e.g., building bridges).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'champion' status implies a stability that discourages further criticism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If this view cannot distinguish between a theory that survived due to luck vs. one that survived due to robustness.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Science is a critical dialogue.
